fields.logicalExtension.con.newArguments.0.text: Revocable consent separates arduous but legitimate service from slavery. Debt repayment, military detention, and employment can restrict choice, yet their legitimacy depends on public justification, proportional limits, review, and a credible route back to agency. Inherited foreign ownership lacks that boundary because one person’s status passes to another without the subject’s authorization. The distinction therefore resists relabeling ownership as mere service without pretending that every constrained relationship is morally equivalent.
